tecnicas.observacao: Pacote em duas fases: avaliação inicial (IE), com geração de testes e de código, e engenharia de prompt evolutiva (EPE), com população inicial de prompts reescritos por LLM, avaliação por taxa de testes gerados aprovados (fitness), seleção aleatória ponderada com elitismo e mutação (por sinônimos via embeddings de palavras, padrão, ou por LLM). Mecanismos: instrucao (persona e diretrizes nos prompts de geração e de reescrita); restricoes (tipos de entrada e saída acrescentados à descrição, limites de palavras, formato de saída dos testes); contexto (assinatura e trecho de código da função fornecidos como insumo); exemplos (exemplo add3Numbers no prompt de testes e casos de teste inseridos na descrição); raciocinio (prompt de testes pede raciocínio passo a passo); feedback (seleção e mutação guiadas pela execução dos testes gerados); amostragem (população de prompts e respostas com seleção por fitness); otimizacao_prompt (evolução automática do prompt). O prompt literal do zero-shot não é descrito no estudo; considerou-se que instrucao e contexto estão na base, e que restricoes (tipos de entrada/saída), exemplos, raciocinio, feedback, amostragem e otimizacao_prompt são acrescentados. O contraste com o zero-shot (Tabela 2) isola o pacote, não um mecanismo. Pacote híbrido: inclui parâmetros de decodificação (temperatura 0,6 na reescrita e 0,0 na geração), tamanho de população e validação sintática de testes por AST, fora do escopo.

Na Tabela 4 é comparado a LLM_as_mutator por substituição de operador (linhas 1 e 2, população 5), sem condição sem mutação; por isso não há contrafactual com e sem o componente.

citacoes.trecho: To address this issue, we propose an alternative approach named Evolutionary Prompt Engineering for Code (EPiC), which leverages a lightweight evolutionary algorithm to refine the original prompts into improved versions that generate high-quality code, with minimal interactions with the LLM.
Candidate prompts are selected from the population using a weighted random selection approach and then mutated to form the next generation of prompts.

The mutation is carried out using two approaches: one utilizes an LLM guided by a prompt that specifies how to perform the mutation, and the other employs vector embeddings of words to find and replace similar words.
Use step-by-step reasoning to validate each test case separately to ensure that all of them have the correct expected output.

citacoes.trecho: A test case is considered valid if it successfully parses into a syntactically correct AST.
For the baseline, we use a zero-shot prompting approach.
Reflexion [29] is a reinforcement-based framework in which language agents learn from linguistic feedback.
LATS [39] (Language Agent Tree Search) is a framework that integrates the planning, acting, and reasoning abilities, inspired by Monte Carlo tree search.
We removed these seed files to ensure fairness, as other baselines do not use any seeds (an initial solution) to boost the performance.
After the initial evaluation, AgentCoder [12] was excluded from further analysis as we found that it is 6 times more expensive than the second most expensive alternative.
The results highlight a clear trade-off: EPiC achieves higher functional correctness at the cost of increased token usage.
This suggests that increasing population size beyond a certain threshold can make the results deviate from the optimal solution and unnecessarily inflates computational cost.
This finding suggests that a simple mutation tool is more cost-effective than an LLM-based tool, although this may not hold for all datasets.
While EA is effective in navigating complex search spaces, it also has drawbacks, such as potential inefficiency when fitness evaluations are expensive and the risk of premature convergence.

One construct threat we face is that our evaluation metrics rely on LLM-generated test cases for intermediate evaluations which could lead to misleading results if these test cases are not representative of the intended tasks.
To ensure a fair evaluation, we deliberately use the same test generation process in both the baselines and EPiC.

One external limitation of this research is that the datasets used (HumanEval+, MBPP+, and BigCodeBench) may not fully represent the diversity of real-world coding tasks, which may limit the generalizability of our findings.
However, we chose LLMs from three different vendors to mitigate this threat.
However, we did not fine-tune our hyper-parameters.

Our evaluation against state-of-the-art (SOTA) LLM-based code generation agents shows that EPiC not only achieves up to 6% improvement in pass@k but is also 2–10 times more cost-effective than the baselines.
Similarly, in MBPP+, EPiC attains a pass@1 of 0.74, slightly outperforming Reflexion (0.72), LATS (0.74), and LDB (0.71).
